roadmap.goal: Slice 03b (value, US-06, ADO #5564): make the metrics dashboard's date pickers actually apply to the two shipped over-time widgets. Optional additive startDate/endDate on `percentiles-over-time` and `process-behavior-over-time` (both team and portfolio scope), filtered on RecordedAt inclusive at both ends and composed server-side onto the existing IQueryable -> threaded through both series query ports and both snapshot repositories -> required startDate/endDate on the two IMetricsService methods -> both hook caches re-keyed from selection-alone to selection-plus-range -> both widgets take the range as props and pick their empty-state copy from it -> BaseMetricsView passes ctx.startDate/ctx.endDate into both widget nodes. Closes milestone-3b Scenarios 16-25. READ-PATH ONLY: recording, the two snapshot tables, the forward-only contract and the demo backfill are all untouched.
roadmap.overview: Single phase (03b), 7 steps in dependency order, pure EXTENSION of shipped slice-01/02/03 code — no new component, no new port, no new route, no new table, NO EF migration. Backbone: 03b-01 repository bounds (both repos; ProcessBehaviorSnapshotRepository gains the GetSeries member it never had, DDD-8) -> 03b-02 both series query ports pass the bounds through -> 03b-03 both controllers x both actions gain the optional params + the inverted-range 400 guard + acceptance scenarios -> 03b-04 IMetricsService/MetricsService + the four FE test doubles the interface change breaks -> 03b-05 both hooks' cache re-key (the slice's named highest-risk item) -> 03b-06 both widgets' props + the DDD-13 empty-state branch + BaseMetricsView wiring -> 03b-07 E2E POM/spec extension + docs row flip + full local gate sweep. RED = RED-by-skip (project convention, DISTILL [REF] RED Mechanism): NUnit ATs / Playwright specs authored with [Ignore("pending — DELIVER (epic-5427 slice-03b)")] / test.skip alongside the minimal signature changes so main always compiles and stays green; each step un-ignores only its own scenarios. Step order is the dependency chain with the riskiest cheap-to-disprove item (the cache re-key) reached as early as its dependencies allow.

open_questions_resolved.pbc_read_path_symmetry: RESOLVED (DDD-8): add `GetSeries(int ownerId, OwnerType ownerType, ProcessBehaviorMetricType metricType, DateOnly? from, DateOnly? to)` to IProcessBehaviorSnapshotRepository and move the predicate + OrderBy down out of ProcessBehaviorSeriesQuery, mirroring the percentiles family. The alternative — growing the predicate inside the query class — is 3 lines cheaper but leaves the two families structurally different for no reason, and slice 04 puts five more metric types through this exact read path. After this step each query class holds only family-specific policy: ResolveHorizon for percentiles, nothing for PBC.
open_questions_resolved.optionality_split: RESOLVED (DDD-11): the WIRE params are optional (`DateTime?`), the FRONTEND service params are required (`Date`). Optional on the wire is what keeps US-06 AC1 true and every shipped acceptance test compiling untouched. Required on the FE is right because ctx.startDate/ctx.endDate are non-nullable `Date` and every sibling service method (getBlockedCountHistory, getFlowEfficiencyInfoForTeam, the percentile reads) is shaped that way — FE optionality would add a branch nothing can reach.
open_questions_resolved.nullable_fromquery: RESOLVED (ci-learnings 2026-05-16): under project-wide `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>` a non-nullable `[FromQuery]` param is REQUIRED by the model binder and a missing value 400s BEFORE the action body runs. The params must therefore be declared `DateTime?` — `DateTime` with a default would still be required-by-default and would break every shipped caller. This is the single most likely way to accidentally violate AC1.
open_questions_resolved.two_independent_bounds: RESOLVED (DDD-10): two independent nullable bounds, not one range object and not an all-or-nothing pair. A lone startDate is a legal 'everything since' request (Scenario 19) and a lone endDate a legal 'everything until'. Consequence for the 400 guard: it fires ONLY when both are present — a single bound has nothing to invert against.
open_questions_resolved.inclusive_boundaries: RESOLVED (US-06 AC2, Scenario 18): `>=` and `<=`, never `>` / `<`. RecordedAt is a DateOnly and the bounds are converted with DateOnly.FromDateTime(x.Date), so there is no time-of-day component to make an exclusive upper bound accidentally correct. This is a prime mutation target (Stryker will flip >= to >) — the boundary test must assert the exact-match day is PRESENT, not merely that the count is plausible.
open_questions_resolved.server_side_composition: RESOLVED (DDD-10, Scenario 25): compose conditionally onto the IQueryable that GetAllByPredicate returns, BEFORE .OrderBy().ToList(). `var q = GetAllByPredicate(base predicate); if (from is not null) q = q.Where(s => s.RecordedAt >= from); if (to is not null) q = q.Where(s => s.RecordedAt <= to); return q.OrderBy(s => s.RecordedAt).ToList();`. Do NOT materialise first and filter in memory, and do NOT put the nullable comparison inside the single base predicate expression — `s.RecordedAt >= (from ?? DateOnly.MinValue)` translates but reads as if the bound were mandatory and defeats the Scenario-25 intent.
open_questions_resolved.cache_key_shape: RESOLVED (DDD-14): both caches become `Record<string, T[]>` keyed on `${selection}|${startISO}|${endISO}`. Keep the existing already-fetched early-return and the existing dep array shape verbatim — it is proven and does not loop (setCache changes cache -> effect re-runs -> early return). Put the Date OBJECTS in the dep array, not derived values: they come from useState<Date> and are referentially stable, so there is no React #185 exposure UNLESS a new inline `new Date()` default is introduced anywhere in the chain. Do not add one.
open_questions_resolved.empty_state_predicate: RESOLVED (DDD-13, US-06 AC5/AC6): `endDate >= today` (compare by calendar day, not by instant) + empty series => the UNCHANGED forward-only copy; `endDate < today` + empty => the new in-range copy. Both shipped E2Es run on the default range, whose end is today, so they keep passing verbatim — that is the regression this predicate is shaped around. Accepted edge, documented not fixed: an owner whose snapshots all predate a window that still ends today reads the forward-only copy.
open_questions_resolved.no_migration: RESOLVED: zero schema delta. No new property on any persisted model, no index change. The CreateMigration script is NOT run this slice.

steps.scenario_name: Range change refetches instead of replaying the cached series (Scenario 22)
steps.implementation_notes: This is where the slice's most likely bug lives, so write the A-then-B stale-cache test BEFORE the key change and watch it fail for the right reason. Derive the key in ONE place per hook (a small module-scope function taking selection + the two dates) so the effect and the read-back cannot disagree — a key computed twice with different formatting is the same stale-series bug wearing a different hat. Use a stable date serialisation (toISOString or a yyyy-MM-dd formatter) rather than String(date), whose output is locale/timezone-shaped. S3776: if the effect's cognitive complexity rises, extract the key builder rather than nesting another branch. If the hooks have no existing test files, create them — do not fold hook assertions into the widget tests, since Scenario 22's seam is the hook.

steps.scenario_name: Both empty-state variants on both widgets (Scenarios 23 + 24)
steps.implementation_notes: Compare endDate to today by CALENDAR DAY, not by instant: ctx.endDate is seeded from `new Date()` and therefore carries a time-of-day, so `endDate >= new Date()` is false a millisecond later and the default range would flip to the in-range copy — that single mistake breaks both shipped E2Es. Normalise both sides to midnight (or compare yyyy-MM-dd strings) and unit-test the same-day case explicitly. Do NOT introduce a `new Date()` prop default on either widget (React #185, and BaseMetricsView always passes the props). The empty-copy comparison helper belongs in the widget, not the hook — the hook has no opinion about copy. ci-learnings: dropping/altering a user-visible label prefix silently kills sibling POM locators, so grep the E2E specs for both copy strings before touching either. The two widgets' empty-state blocks will now look similar but they are NOT identical (different constants, different series types) — resist extracting a shared component in this slice; that is a refactor commit if it is worth doing at all.

steps.implementation_notes: Window arithmetic: the demo backfill covers [today-14, today-1] and the team default window is 30 days, so the default view contains the whole backfill and narrowing to ~7 days reliably reduces the point count. For the in-range-copy scenario pick a window entirely before today-14 (e.g. [today-60, today-45]) — that guarantees empty AND ends before today. Set the range through the dashboard's own pickers via the existing sibling-widget POM path, or via the startDate/endDate URL search params that BaseMetricsView already parses (:1203/:1208) — the URL route is more deterministic and avoids a date-picker interaction flake; prefer it and say so in the spec. ci-learnings: MUI-X dashed/solid selectors and shared test-ids are strict-mode traps — scope every new locator to its widget container, and remember MUI strips data-testid from ICONS in production builds.
